name: Fault-equivalent four-legged spider
summary: A phase-free four-legged Z-spider is fault-equivalent to a 4-cycle of three-legged Z-spiders.
description:
A four-legged Z-spider can be replaced by a square of four three-legged Z-spiders, one for each leg. This decomposes a weight-four measurement into spiders of degree three while preserving fault equivalence, in contrast to the naive decomposition into a chain or star of spiders, in which a single flip can spread to two legs.

Fault equivalence is with respect to *edge-flip noise*: every edge of the diagram can suffer a Pauli $X$, $Y$ or $Z$ flip of weight 1. The four spiders of the square form a detecting region, so an odd number of $X$-flips on the internal edges is detected, while an even number of $X$-flips and all $Z$-flips can be pushed to the outer legs without increasing their weight. The rule follows by [spider fusion](../spider-fusion/) and [self-loop removal](../self-loop-removal/), but fusion in general is not fault-equivalent.
